key_insight: FeTS++ 2027 expands federated medical imaging benchmarking by adding a federated classification task and moving the challenge infrastructure to NVFlare across a larger, more diverse multi-institutional cohort.
clinical_relevance: The challenge aims to improve how tumor segmentation and tumor-type classification models are developed across hospitals without centralizing patient data, supporting more realistic deployment of AI in neuro-oncology.
method: Federated learning across institutions with data kept locally
Task 1: aggregate per-institution segmentation models for tumor segmentation
Task 2: classify glioma vs meningioma under the same federated protocol
evidence_signal: The abstract describes a multi-institutional MRI dataset spanning North America, Europe, Asia, and Africa, with methods ranked by model utility and an efficiency-aware score.
watch_item: Classification is heavily confounded by site of origin, so site bias and cross-institution generalization are major concerns when interpreting results.
paper_title: The Federated Tumor Segmentation and Classification (FeTS++) Challenge
